mechanism: The University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers ask households whether they expect business conditions to improve or worsen. Rising expectations are read as a sign of stronger spending and risk-on equity conditions; falling expectations as the opposite. The procyclical prior holds SPY when expectations are high or rising.
key_finding: On today's Michigan Expected Business Conditions values (no archive of past values exists), the rule selected on in-sample data uses zscore_60m at L9 (IS Sharpe 0.94) with test-period Sharpe 0.66 versus buy-and-hold 0.93.
caveats: No public archive of past values of this series exists, so the backtest uses today's values; any revision would add hindsight that cannot be measured.
The strategy is search-selected and needs fresh holdout validation.
The Data Master series ends 2025-09, so the test period ends there.
The rule published on the main site (20260912) was the highest out-of-sample Sharpe with fixed lags (the test period was used to choose it); it is replaced here.
narrative_summary: The share of University of Michigan respondents expecting better business conditions is tested as a procyclical sentiment overlay for SPY: hold equity when expectations are favourable.
